title: Ronaldo's Last World Cup Ends — And a Co-Host's Goalkeeper Meltdown

scenes.voiceover: Two Round of 16 storylines from the same day — one ended a legend's World Cup, the other ended a co-host's tournament with a goalkeeping disaster.
scenes.mainText: ONE DAY. TWO WORLD CUP DISASTERS.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: A split, dramatic stadium scene at dusk, two different football matches happening in parallel, cinematic painterly illustration, no text, no watermark

scenes.voiceover: Mikel Merino scored the winner in the first minute of stoppage time — 90 plus 1.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: A footballer in a red kit sprinting in explosive celebration after scoring a last-second winning goal, stadium floodlights, roaring crowd, cinematic painterly illustration, no text, no watermark

scenes.voiceover: Before kickoff, Cristiano Ronaldo had already said it: 'This will be my last World Cup, but let's hope tomorrow isn't my last game.'
scenes.mainText: "THIS WILL BE MY LAST WORLD CUP"

scenes.voiceover: After the loss, he confirmed it: 'It's been my last World Cup, yes. But now I will have time to think, stay with my family, and life continues.'
Minutes later, Portugal's head coach Roberto Martínez announced his resignation, effective immediately.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: A football manager in a suit standing alone in an empty stadium tunnel, head down, walking away, somber and final, cinematic painterly illustration, no text, no watermark

scenes.voiceover: Meanwhile, in Seattle, a World Cup co-host was falling apart in a completely different way.
USA goalkeeper Matt Freese came out of his area, hesitated, and booted the ball straight to Belgium's Hans Vanaken, who fired it back in from thirty yards for the 57th-minute goal.
scenes.mainText: USA'S GOALKEEPER GIFTED BELGIUM THE THIRD GOAL
scenes.backgroundPrompt: A goalkeeper in a white kit standing alone in an open goal area, head in hands, stadium lights above, a moment of visible despair, cinematic painterly illustration, no text, no watermark

scenes.voiceover: The United States became the final World Cup co-host to be eliminated — after Canada fell to Morocco, and Mexico fell to England.
scenes.mainText: USA: THE LAST CO-HOST STANDING — NOW ELIMINATED
